Definition: from G1909 and G3687; to name further, i.e. denominate:--call.
BiblicalUsage: Eponomázō means to be called by a name — to bear a name as your own. It occurs just once, where Paul says the Jew who relies on the law is called a Jew. The name is a claim, and Paul tests whether the life matches it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe eponomázō cuts straight to the point: a name you carry is a claim you have to live up to.
